matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can become an X (two crossing diagonals) and vice‑versa by moving a single diagonal stick within the same character, changing its value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral X (10) or V (5) appears and a value adjustment of exactly 5 is required.
matchstick.example: Changing the last X in XIX to V yields XIV, reducing the total by 5.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides of the equation; the difference indicates how much the total must change, guiding which numeral or operator to modify.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, before considering specific stick moves.
matchstick.example: LHS 19 vs RHS 14 gives a discrepancy of 5, suggesting a change that alters the value by 5.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The equality sign consists of two horizontal sticks; after moving a stick it must still represent a valid operator (=, +, or -). Do not turn it into an invalid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick move might involve the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Leaving both horizontals untouched ensures the sign stays '=', keeping the equation structure.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, each affected symbol must still be a recognized Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a legal operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any proposed stick relocation, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X must not leave a lone diagonal, which would be invalid.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks retain their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, and a diagonal cannot become vertical.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When deciding where to place a moved stick.
matchstick.example: A vertical stick from '+' can only be placed where a vertical is needed, e.g., to form an I.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator is allowed only if the new shape corresponds to a legal operator (+, -, =). For example, removing the vertical from '+' yields '-', which is valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick is moved from or to an operator.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' to an I turns '+' into '-' and creates a new I.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick relocation, recalculate the Arabic values of all numerals and re‑evaluate the arithmetic to verify equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, before accepting the solution.
matchstick.example: After turning X to V, recompute LHS from 19 to 14 and confirm it matches RHS.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign while the removed stick can be placed elsewhere as a vertical.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation needs a subtraction instead of addition, or when a vertical stick is needed for another numeral.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' to form an extra I changes '+' to '-' and adds 1 to the RHS.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be taken from one character (decreasing its value) and attached to another (increasing its value), achieving a net adjustment that balances the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy cannot be fixed by a single intra‑character change.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an X (10→5) to a V (5→10) keeps the total unchanged, useful in other puzzles.

matchstick.title: Discrepancy‑5 heuristic for X↔V adjustment
matchstick.principle: If the computed difference between sides is exactly 5 (or –5) and the equation contains an X or V, the quickest fix is often to change that X to V (or V to X) by moving a single diagonal stick, adjusting the value by ±5 without affecting other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, if it equals 5 (or –5) and an X or V is present that can be altered.
matchstick.example: LHS 19 vs RHS 14 (difference 5) → turn the last X in XIX into V, yielding XIV = XII + II.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable symbols and forgets that vertical, horizontal, and diagonal sticks are distinct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always track the orientation of each stick; a moved stick must keep its original orientation when placed.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model seeks any place to move a stick and may inadvertently alter the '=' sign, forgetting its special role.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Treat the equality sign as immutable unless the move still leaves it as a valid operator (=, +, or -).

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on numeric balance and neglects the requirement that each symbol remain a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every affected character matches a known Roman numeral or allowed operator.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may move sticks to operators without checking the resulting shape, producing non‑operator symbols.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure any operator modification results in a recognized operator (+, -, =).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes jumps to a stick move without first quantifying how the values differ, leading to ineffective changes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the Arabic values of both sides first; the discrepancy guides which value adjustments are needed.
